summary_html: **CAPTA §5106a(c)** requires every state to maintain **Citizen Review Panels** that evaluate CPS policies. Project Milk Carton checks whether panels are active, independent, and publicly reporting.

key_cases.case_name: Union Leader Corp. v. N.H. Dep't of Safety
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the dismissal of a Right-to-Know suit for State Police records of the response to the Sununu Youth Services Center, clarifying that juvenile confidentiality under RSA 169-B:35 reaches records held by non-court agencies only to the extent disclosure would run counter to the purpose of rehabilitating delinquent minors, and remanded for that determination and for consideration of redaction.
key_cases.relevance: Independent review of child welfare and juvenile justice practice depends on the redacted-record access the court recognizes here.
key_cases.quote: This refinement effectuates the juvenile delinquency statutes’ purpose of rehabilitating delinquent minors while also ensuring “the greatest possible public access to the actions, discussions and records of all public bodies.”

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the 'reasonable efforts' requirement of the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act, 42 U.S.C. § 671(a)(15), does not create a right enforceable by beneficiaries either through 42 U.S.C. § 1983 or by implied private right of action.
key_cases.relevance: Citizen review panels and similar oversight bodies fill the accountability gap Suter leaves by removing private enforcement of federal standards.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents

key_cases.holding: The court held that when the division finds a report of abuse or neglect 'founded' and records that determination in the central registry it adjudicates the subject's status and must, under Part I, Article 15 of the State Constitution, give written notice of the determination, its reasons, the identification of the named perpetrator, and the rights of access and administrative challenge; the division's notice here was constitutionally inadequate.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion's warning about governmental possession and use of inaccurate child protection data is the doctrinal basis for independent review of agency recordkeeping.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the notification procedures employed by the division did not afford the Bagleys the protections required by part I, article 15 of the New Hampshire Constitution
